aAbout: EarthCam runs a network of live webcams anchored by famous places — Times Square in New York is the signature view — organised into destination pages and EarthCam TV channels that package cameras into themed streams. Alongside the free consumer network it sells professional construction-camera systems to businesses, with managed hardware, archiving and time-lapse. Many public cameras are watchable free in the browser and in its mobile apps, with weather information shown alongside some cameras.
aStrengths: EarthCam is the deeper platform for famous places: a large, long-running network of scenic and tourist cameras anchored by Times Square, curated viewing through EarthCam TV, and professional construction-camera services with managed hardware, archiving and time-lapse for commercial clients. For watching a specific famous place — or for a business that needs a camera installed and managed — EarthCam's camera-specific depth and history beat a travel directory.
bAbout: SkylineWebcams is a webcam directory based in Italy hosting thousands of scenic and travel webcams worldwide — beaches, cities, landscapes, volcanoes, ski areas and ports — organised by place and category. Its catalogue is particularly deep in Italy and other popular tourist destinations, where many cameras have streamed for years. Watching is free with advertising; an optional Premium tier removes the ads and unlocks the interactive map, favourites and search.
bStrengths: SkylineWebcams is the deeper travel directory: thousands of scenic webcams organised by place and category — beaches, cities, landscapes, volcanoes and more — with particularly strong coverage of Italy and popular tourist destinations, where many cameras have run for years. If the goal is browsing holiday destinations or checking a specific beach or piazza before a trip, its travel-focused curation is the better fit, and its Premium tier is unusually cheap.
betterAnswer: Neither is better in the abstract; they curate different worlds. EarthCam concentrates on famous places and runs a professional camera business alongside; SkylineWebcams spreads wider across travel destinations, especially in Europe, and charges a token amount to remove ads. People who mostly watch one iconic place pick EarthCam; people who wander between beaches and towns pick SkylineWebcams. Many webcam fans use both — and use a globe-based network when they want cameras combined with live flights, weather and events, which neither directory offers.

intro: EarthCam and SkylineWebcams are the two names most people land on when they want to watch the world through live webcams. EarthCam is the American network famous for landmark cameras — Times Square above all — with curated TV-style channels and a sideline in professional construction cameras. SkylineWebcams is an Italian directory of thousands of scenic and travel webcams, especially strong around the Mediterranean. Both are free to watch; they differ in what they curate, how they charge, and how you browse.
pricingA: Watching EarthCam's public cameras is free. Its professional construction-camera services, hardware and business offerings are paid and typically quoted per project — there is no consumer subscription comparable to a premium tier.
pricingB: Free to watch, supported by advertising. Premium (official price, checked October 2026) costs €9.50/year or €3.90 for 3 months, with no automatic renewal. It removes ads and adds favourites, the interactive map, search and extra features.

verdictA: Choose EarthCam if you want the famous views — Times Square and other landmark cameras — TV-style curated channels, or professional construction-camera services for a business site.
verdictB: Choose SkylineWebcams if you browse by destination — beaches, resorts, Italian and Mediterranean towns — and want a very cheap way to remove ads and unlock map browsing.
worldEye: If what you actually want is to browse the planet rather than a directory, WorldEye puts 74,229 public cameras on a free interactive 3D globe — across 105 countries — together with live flights, satellites, ships, weather, earthquakes and wildfires in the same view. There is nothing to install and no signup: the map is free, and an optional Pro tier ($7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year) adds the OSINT toolkit and intel feeds. It will not replace EarthCam's construction services or SkylineWebcams' Italian beach depth, but for sheer camera breadth in one place it is the larger network.
